svg.text: Why leaders struggle with improvement: the capability trap
How the struggles feed each other, and how the green actions turn the vicious circle into a virtuous one
No one else can do it
properly, even if it takes longer
even if it costs more at first
● Use the slack: appoint someone to do the improvement legwork, and help people adapt to new routines
● Learn from the past and from outside: bright spots and dark spots. Appoint a remembrancer to record what was learned, and why, in the organisation’s records, not just people’s heads
● Think long term: improvements take years, and the market keeps changing
● Let the improvement helper use AI to draft productivity tools, procedures, checklists and rules, checked with the people who do the work
Flip the vicious circle (R1) into a virtuous one (R3): work on the green actions

g.text: an action that breaks the vicious circle
Core loop after Repenning and Sterman (2001) · stepchangeanalysis.com
